key_insight: LE-DM reconstructs volumetric PTV velocity fields with moving solid boundaries by masking the domain and enforcing signed-distance-based boundary kinematics inside a single constrained solve.
engineering_relevance: It enables boundary-consistent, divergence-free velocity and gradient estimates near moving bodies, improving pressure and hydrodynamic force evaluation in particle-tracking experiments.
method: Time-dependent signed-distance mask splits the grid into fluid, boundary shell, and solid interior.
Particle data, incompressibility, prescribed surface velocity, and regularization are solved together on the masked domain.
Works for stationary, translating, rotating, multiple, and deforming bodies with only a signed-distance field plus surface velocity.
evidence_signal: Validated on an oscillating-sphere analytical case, CFD-derived synthetic tracks, and a tomographic-PTV rising-sphere experiment, with surface kinematics enforced to solver tolerance and first-cell error reduced from 14% to 3% in the analytical test.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on having a reliable signed-distance field and prescribed surface velocity; errors in boundary motion or mask placement could degrade near-wall reconstruction.
paper_title: Dynamic masking for boundary-aware velocity reconstruction in volumetric particle tracking with moving solids
